I farm 600 mu, so I will not do things too fancy, but I will not farm by guesswork either. I have done this for 20 years, and at my age I mostly start from what worked the year before, then I adjust a little for price, water, and the crop. In Quzhou County, with well irrigation, I will still put the main area into the wheat-maize rotation because that is the safest money and the machines run smoothly on big blocks. I will keep some cotton because it can still bring cash if I manage the insects on time, and I will keep a smaller stevia area because it needs tighter management and more labor. Since fertilizer is expensive, I will not throw it blindly, but I would still rather feed the crop enough than save a little money and lose yield. For wheat and maize, I will stay close to the rates that have worked on irrigated land here, with wheat fed a bit heavier up front and maize pushed at jointing. Cotton needs more potassium and more pesticide trips, and stevia I will keep cleaner and more even because quality matters. Since I have well water, I will use irrigation as my safety valve: wheat 3 times, maize 2 times, cotton 4 times, stevia 4 times. For area, I will keep 450 mu in wheat-maize rotation, 100 mu in cotton, and 50 mu in stevia this year.
